them?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPHARMACOLOGIC REPLACEMENT :\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIncreased vascular permeability in acute pancreatitis causes the loss of intravenous fluid and reduces plasma volume. In severe cases, in patients with massive ascites, pleural effusion, and retroperitoneal and mesenteric edema, circulating plasma volume decreases markedly. Hypovolemia may lead to shock and acute renal failure, and, because hypovolemic shock may impair the pancreatic microcirculation and promote pancreatic ischemia and necrosis, restoration and maintenance of plasma volume is crucial in severe acute pancreatitis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2.ANTIBIOTICS : No role in non necrotizing \/ sterile pancreatitis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3.TRAMADOL : For pain management\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E4.ZOFER : For vomitings\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E5.PANTOP : To prevent gastritis and further damage to pancreas by inhibiting gastrin\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E6.LASIX : For fluid overload\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E7.NEBULIZATION : For wheezing and Please chart out the sequence of events timeline between the manifestations of each of these problems and current outcomes.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EANATOMICAL LOCATIONS WITH ETIOLOGY:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1)pedal edema with abdominal distention with sob suggestive of right heart failure or renal failure\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EB)etilogy of rt heart failure\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK459381\/\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EChronic conditions of pressure overload may lead to RVF. These include:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;* Primary pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and secondary pulmonary hypertension (PH) as seen in chronic-obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) or pulmonary fibrosis)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Congenital heart disease (pulmonic stenosis, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, or a systemic RV).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe following conditions result in volume overload causing RVF:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Valvular insufficiency (tricuspid or pulmonic)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Congenital heart disease with a shunt (atrial septal defect (ASD) or anomalous pulmonary venous return (APVR)).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnother important mechanism that leads to RVF is intrinsic RV myocardial disease.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;This includes:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* RV ischemia or infarct\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Infiltrative diseases such as amyloidosis or sarcoidosis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia (ARVD)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Cardiomyopathy\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Microvascular disease.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELastly, RVF may be caused by impaired filling which is seen in the following conditions:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Constrictive pericarditis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Tricuspid stenosis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Systemic vasodilatory shock\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Cardiac tamponade\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Superior vena cava syndrome\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E* Hypovolemia.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESEQUENCE OF EVENTS:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- (5 years)\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- 1st Episode GTCS (3 years) \u0026amp; AF with HFpEF\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- 2nd Episode GTCS (2 swelling since 2 months\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/nairaditya97.blogspot.com\/2020\/11\/31-yr-old-male-with-bl-pedal-edema-with.html?m=1\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ea) Where are the different anatomical locations of the patient's problems and what are the different etiologic possibilities for them? Please chart out the sequence of events timeline between the manifestations of each of these problems and current outcomes.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1.Patient is a chronic alcoholic which causes wet beri beri(heart failure due to thiamine deficiency)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2.peripheral neuropathy due to thiamine deficiency\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWet beriberi is one of the clinical syndromes associated with thiamine deficiency. Thiamine, in its phosphorylated form thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP), is the precursor for the cofactor of both pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, which are both key enzymes of the Krebs cycle. The Krebs cycle is an essential part of aerobic glucose metabolism. A decrease in the activity of these 2 enzymes due to thiamine deficiency may lead to the tissue accumulation of pyruvate and lactate.[1] Moreover, the accumulation of pyruvate and lactate decreases peripheral resistance and increases venous blood flow, increasing the cardiac preload. Increased preload and myocardial dysfunction ultimately leads to congestive heart failure.[2,3] Wet beriberi mainly triggers right heart failure.[4–6] The moderate pulmonary hypertension is common for wet beriberi patient.[3,4,7\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC5851725\/\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EEVENTS TIME LINE:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Alcohol \u0026amp; khaini (3 years)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Pins and needles (1 year)\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Palpitations and sob on exertion (8 months)\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- PND (6months)\u0026nbsp;\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Sexual disturbance and constipation (3months)\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Pedal edema and Scrotal edema(2 months)\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E- Admitted\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECURRENT OUTCOME:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECompletly relieved of his symptoms as the wet beriberi resolved.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EB) What are the pharmacological and non pharmacological interventions used in the management of this patient and what are the efficacy of each one of them?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPHARMACOLOGIC :\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1.LASIX : Mortality: 3 placebo-controlled trials (n=221) reported data; the OR was 0.25 (95% confidence interval, CI: 0.07, 0.84, P=0.03), representing an absolute risk reduction of 8% in mortality in patients treated with diuretics compared to placebo.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWorsening of heart failure: 4 placebo-controlled trials (n=448) and 4 active-controlled trials (n=177) reported data. The OR was 0.31 (95% CI: 0.15, 0.62, P=0.001) for the placebo-controlled trials and 0.34 (95% CI:0.10, 1.21, P=0.10) for the active-controlled trials.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK69174\/\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2.THIAMINE : In the study by Schoenenberger and colleagues (n=9), patients who took thiamine had 3.30% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.63%, 5.97%) greater LVEF compared to those on placebo.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ELikewise, Shimon et al reported that thiamine resulted in 2.20% greater LVEF than the placebo group (n=29), although the extra improvement was not significant (95% CI: −18.97, 23.37%).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIn our meta analysis, thiamine supplementation resulted in a significantly improved net change in LVEF (3.28%, 95% CI: 0.64%, 5.93%) compared with placebo.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC3865826\/#:~:text=Compared%20with%20placebo%20(2%20trials,0.64%25%2C%205.93%25).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3.TELMISARTAN : For afterload reduction in heart failure\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENON PHARMACOLOGIC the comment box is welcome.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E55 year old man, fruit seller at NTR nagar Hyderabad presented to our casualty with the complaints of\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESwelling of both his lower limbs since 4 months\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EFacial puffiness since 2 weeks\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ECough since 3 days\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHe was previously working as a coolie at suryapet and got married to a farmer. He has 4 children, 3 daughters and a son. He has been drinking alcohol since 30 years, takes around 90ml of whiskey once a week. His last drink was 2 months ago.He used to even smoke around 5 beedis per day 20 years back.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAround 20 years back, he got diagnosed to be a diabetic on regular checkup and has been on regular medications ever since.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOne year back, when he went for a routine diabetic checkup he got diagnosed to be a hypertensive but hasn’t been taking medications regularly.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E8 months back, he developed blebs over his right and left foot after walking on a hot marble at suryapet. Subsequently he developed bilateral swelling of his lower limbs extending upto his thigh over a month. He visited a local hospital where he received certains medications after which which the swelling got resolved.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESince 4 months he started noticing swelling of both his lower limbs which progressed gradually to his thigh. Though he tells us no complaints of hematuria, frothy urine, dypsnea on exertion ,reduced urine out put, chest pain. 2 weeks back he started to notice facial puffiness.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2weeks back, one day he had giddiness after which he was taken to a hospital where he was put on 25% dextrose and was told that he was hypoglycaemic and OHAs were put on hold. In the coming days he even developed fever with chills after which he underwent screening for COVID 19 which came out to be negative. He was admitted in a local hospital and has apparently received certain antibiotics ( not mentioned which though) and was even on Tab Dytor plus. Since 3 days he has also been complaining of cough with scanty mucoid expectoration.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOn presentation, he was
